chapter_name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
learning_objective: 🎯 Master the mechanics of spinning objects! Learn how to find the balance point of any system, calculate twisting forces, and understand why ice skaters spin faster when they pull their arms in.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Every object or system of particles has a unique balance point where its entire mass can be assumed to be concentrated. If you apply a force exactly at this point, the object will move in a straight line without spinning!

Just as Force causes straight-line motion, Torque ($\tau = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{F}$) causes rotational motion. It depends on the force applied AND how far you apply it from the pivot point (which is why door handles are placed far from the hinges).

The rotational equivalent of mass. It measures how hard it is to start or stop an object from spinning ($I = \sum mr^2$). It depends not just on the total mass, but on how that mass is distributed away from the axis of rotation.

If no external torque acts on a spinning system, its angular momentum ($L = I\omega$) remains perfectly constant. If the Moment of Inertia ($I$) decreases, the angular velocity ($\omega$) MUST increase to compensate!
When a wheel rolls without slipping, it is doing two things at once: translating (moving forward) and rotating (spinning). The total kinetic energy is the sum of translational KE and rotational KE.

fun_activity.title: ⛸️ The Spinning Skater Effect
fun_activity.instructions: Sit on a swivel office chair with your arms stretched out holding heavy books. Have a friend gently spin you. Now, quickly pull the books tight to your chest. You will instantly start spinning much faster due to the Conservation of Angular Momentum!

exam_tips: 📌 Master the Perpendicular and Parallel Axis Theorems. They are guaranteed to be tested in numericals for finding the Moment of Inertia of rings, discs, and spheres.
📌 Remember that Torque and Angular Momentum are cross products, meaning their direction is given by the Right-Hand Rule and is perpendicular to the plane of motion.
📌 In pure rolling motion on a stationary surface, the velocity of the lowest point of contact with the ground is exactly zero.
quick_recap: ⭐ The center of mass of a system moves purely as if all external forces were applied directly to it.
⭐ Mass concentrated far from the axis creates a higher Moment of Inertia, making it harder to spin.
⭐ Angular momentum is conserved in the universe, just like linear momentum and energy.
